general_information.Syllabus Name: Idea & Script Development _Phát triển ý tưởng và kịch bản
general_information.Description: Description: This course builds the skills to turn ideas into industry-standard scripts for short films and TVCs. Students analyze and apply narrative structure and character arcs; produce a 3–5 minute short-film script and a 30–45 second TVC script/storyboard; and collaborate through critique and pitching. AI tools may support ideation and drafting, but usage must be documented and ethical, with originality and authorship maintained.
general_information.StudentTasks: '- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance > - Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

description: Description: This course builds the skills to turn ideas into industry-standard scripts for short films and TVCs. Students analyze and apply narrative structure and character arcs; produce a 3–5 minute short-film script and a 30–45 second TVC script/storyboard; and collaborate through critique and pitching. AI tools may support ideation and drafting, but usage must be documented and ethical, with originality and authorship maintained.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Explain the role of scripts in film/TVC production pipelines.
Analyze and apply script structures and methods to transform ideas into scripts.
Analyze and apply TVC storytelling structures to craft 30–45s concepts.
Develop compelling characters and coherent character arcs appropriate to genre and theme.

Write a complete short-film script (3–5 minutes ≈ 3–5 pages) and a TVC script/storyboard (30–45s) using industry-standard screenplay format (scene headings, action, dialogue, transitions) and iterative revisions.
Integrate AI-enhanced tools for ideation, drafting, and refinement, critically evaluate and document usage to ensure originality, authorship, and ethical compliance.
Work professionally, independently and in teams; meet deadlines, incorporate feedback, and communicate effectively in critiques/pitches.

assessments.Note: Participation grade will be given based on students' attendance, students' attitude, preparation, contribution of discussions

assessments.Category: Practice 1 (individual work): Script for Short Film (3-5 mins)
assessments.Question Type: Write a 3–5 minute short film script that demonstrates idea development, structure, and character building, while practicing storytelling and responsible use of AI for ideation and refinement.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: • Knowledge: Principles of short film scriptwriting, including idea development, narrative structure, and character creation. • Skills: Applying storytelling techniques to write a complete short film script (3–5 minutes), developing coherent plots and characters, and using AI responsibly for ideation and refinement.
assessments.Grading Guide: 1. Presentation_Script Analysis of a Short Animated Film: Choose a short animated film and present an analysis explaining the script’s role, the development of its idea and theme, and its three-act structure. 2. From Logline to Character Development: Expand a selected logline into a premise/synopsis and a compact character bible. Define goals, conflicts, and clear character arcs that align with the theme and genre. (AI may support ideation/refinement; document usage.) 3. Script Structure (3-Act Summary): Write a clear outline of the story in three acts (setup, confrontation, resolution. Specify turning points, stakes, and causal links. 4. Complete Scriptwriting: Write a full 3–5 page screenplay in industry format, revising from feedback and staying consistent with the outline. Submit the final draft with a brief revision log and AI process evidence.
assessments.Note: Submission Files: 1. Presentation slides for the animated film analysis (PPT/PDF) 2. Word file containing all development steps (loglines, idea development answers, 3-act structure summary, and character profiles) (.docx) 3. Final short film script (Word file, 3–5 A4 pages, correct screenplay format with proper margins, font, size, capitalization rules, and appropriate screenplay writing style) (.docx) 4. AI Usage Report: Screenshots or notes showing AI-generated references/plot suggestions, with a short explanation of how they supported refinement (.docx/PDF) In-Class Work: 1. Presentation of the script analysis of a chosen short animated film. 2. Peer and instructor feedback on loglines, 3-act structures, and character designs. 3. Drafting and revising script sections during In-class sessions.

assessments.Question Type: Create a 30–45 second TVC script that demonstrates clear structure, effective character design, and a strong brand message. Apply storytelling principles with professionalism, and use AI tools for ideation, storyboarding, demo video creation, or refinement while ensuring originality.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: • Knowledge: Understand 30–45s TVC storytelling and structure, character/arc essentials, and industry-standard script/storyboard conventions and timing. • Skills: Turn a brief into a logline/beat sheet and produce an industry-standard TVC script/storyboard with clear structure and characters; use AI for ideation, storyboarding, demo, or refinement while documenting usage and maintaining originality.
assessments.Grading Guide: 1. Presentation: Brand Research Conduct a brand research study that analyzes the brand’s history, values, USP, target audience, competitors, and positioning. Use AI tools at the enhanced level to support information synthesis, data analysis, and creative exploration (e.g., generating moodboards, slogans, or initial ideas). 2. TVC Scriptwriting - TVC Storyboard - Demo video for the TVC Using insights from your Brand Research, create a 30–45s TVC with: • Script in industry format (scene headings, action, dialogue/VO, transitions). • Storyboard (≈8–12 frames) with captions and timings. • Demo/animatic video (30–45s, MP4) showing pacing and key beats. AI use: Use AI for ideation, rewrites, shot listing/storyboarding, and demo assembly. Document all AI usage (tools, prompts, sources, edits) and ensure originality and authorship.
assessments.Note: Submission Files: 1. Brand Research Report: Brand analysis, audience research, competitor analysis, narrative outline, AI usage report (enhanced level) (.docx/PDF) 2. Final TVC Script (docx/PDF) 3. AI-generated storyboard and AI Usage Report (.docx/PDF) 4. AI-Generated Demo Video and AI Usage Report: MP4 file (.mp4), resolution min. 720p. In-Class Work: 1. Presentation of the script analysis of a chosen short animated film. 2. Instructor feedback on brand research, TVC structure, and AI usage 3. Drafting and revising script sections during In-class sessions.
